headline: Fragrant rice hits record prices in Bangladesh; up Tk 60-80 per kg in a month
summary: The price of fragrant rice has surged by Tk 60-80 per kg in a month, reaching record highs. Traders attribute the increase to rising exports and a resulting local shortage, with some alleging illegal hoarding.
details: Various types of fragrant rice are being sold at record prices in the Bangladeshi market. Over the past month, prices have increased by Tk 60 to Tk 80 per kilogram, depending on the variety.

Market observations reveal a sharp rise in the price of loose polao rice. Varieties that cost Tk 160 per kg a few months ago are now being sold for Tk 170-200. Packaged rice was already priced at Tk 210 per kg.
Shopkeepers explain that the increased export of fragrant rice has created a slight shortage in the local market. This shortage is directly impacting the current price surge.
Rice wholesalers complain that the heightened demand for Chinigura rice among expatriates has boosted export requirements. This situation has led some individuals to engage in illegal hoarding.

A. H. M. Shafiquzzaman, President of CAB (Consumers Association of Bangladesh), stated that there is no actual shortage of rice in the market. He suspects that dishonest traders are creating an artificial crisis to maximize profits.
According to data from the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB), a total of 23,959 tons of fragrant rice have been approved for export in two phases during the 2025-26 fiscal year.

headline: FIFA scraps private investment plan after fierce global backlash from football officials
summary: World football's governing body FIFA has abandoned its proposal to allow private investment in flagship events, following widespread condemnation from continental federations and a senior advisor's resignation.
details: World football governing body FIFA announced today it has scrapped its plan to allow private investment in flagship events. This decision comes after fierce backlash from football officials worldwide.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino stated that the organization's purpose has always been to unite and improve. The proposed plan, floated earlier this week, aimed to raise up to $4.2 billion.

The plan involved a new FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion, intended to run events like the World Cup. It promised a one-off payment of $20 million to each of FIFA's 211 member associations by early 2027.

Additionally, the project proposed increasing funding allocation for the 2027-2030 cycle from $8 million to $20 million per member association. However, the idea of private investors holding even a small stake was quickly condemned.

European football's governing body UEFA declared that none of its national teams would participate in any FIFA competition if these proposals remained. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and North American and Caribbean federation (CONCACAF) also voiced strong opposition.

A significant blow to Infantino came with the resignation of senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro, who called the idea "a bad deal for FIFA's member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game."

In a statement, Infantino clarified that the project was conceived to strengthen member associations and would only proceed with majority support. He acknowledged that the plan had created divisions, which were no longer in the interest of the initial objective.
